newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-LIONS NAME BOBBY ROSS HEAD COACH.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-LIONS NAME BOBBY ROSS HEAD COACH.

text.p: Bobby Ross, who guided the San Diego Chargers to the Super Bowl two years ago, was named the new head coach of the Detroit Lions on Monday.
Terms were not disclosed, but Ross has reportedly agreed to a five-year, $7.5 million.

Ross, who resigned as coach of the Chargers on January 3 over what was termed "philosophical differences" with general manager Bobby Beathard, replaces Wayne Fontes, who was fired right after the season.
Ross, whose Chargers posted an 8-8 mark last season, compiled a 47-33 overall record in five years with San Diego.
Under Ross, the Chargers were 3-3 in playoff games, including a 49-26 loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Super Bowl XXIX.
Before taking over in San Diego, Ross guided Georgia Tech to a share of college football's national championship in 1990.
Fontes was fired on December 26 after eight seasons as coach. He took the Lions to the playoffs in four of the last six years, but had just one playoff victory.
Detroit started the 1996 season with four wins in six games, but lost nine of its next 10 and finished 5-11.
